package_info.why_malicious: This report is a high-level analysis of software supply chain risks and does not describe a specific malicious package or code. Instead, it highlights the increasing sophistication of supply chain attacks, including code tampering, backdoor insertion, and the exploitation of open-source repositories and CI/CD pipelines. The macro-level reasoning is that attackers are targeting trusted software distribution channels to introduce malicious code, often bypassing traditional vulnerability-focused defenses.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected code changes in trusted or widely used open-source packages
Insertion of backdoors or cryptominers into legitimate projects
Tampering with code at any stage of the CI/CD pipeline
Privilege escalation or abuse of privileged accounts in development environments
file_indicators: Unexpected modifications to package files (e.g., setup.py, package.json, workflow YAMLs)
Presence of unauthorized scripts or binaries in build artifacts
Unexplained changes in SBOMs (Software Bill of Materials)
network_indicators: Outbound connections from build or CI/CD environments to unknown or suspicious domains
Exfiltration of sensitive data (e.g., credentials, tokens) to external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized or unexpected changes in source code repositories, especially in widely used open-source packages. Implement continuous integrity checks and tamper detection throughout the CI/CD pipeline, including post-build and post-deployment stages. Analyze SBOMs for unexpected components or changes. Monitor network activity from build and deployment environments for signs of data exfiltration or communication with suspicious domains. Regularly audit privileged accounts and access controls in development and CI/CD systems.
